## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Don't merge this yet. The containment check in `preview` compares paths only as text. It never resolves them, so a relative path containing `..` gets past the check and reads files outside the home directory. The added test only checks that an absolute path is rejected, so it misses this traversal. The policy manifest lists no policy files.

## Critical
- app/paths.py:12 — correctness — `preview` builds `candidate = Path(home) / relative` and then checks `candidate.is_relative_to(Path(home))`. `is_relative_to` only compares path parts as text. It does not resolve `..` or symlinks. So `preview("/home/u", "../../etc/passwd")` produces `/home/u/../../etc/passwd`, which passes the check, and `read_text()` then returns the first 200 characters of `/etc/passwd`. A symlink inside home that points outside it also passes. The test at `tests/test_paths.py:19-20` only covers an absolute `relative` argument, which `Path.__truediv__` already turns into a path outside `home`, so the test can't catch this bug. Could you compare resolved paths instead, e.g. `base = Path(home).resolve(); candidate = (base / relative).resolve(); if not candidate.is_relative_to(base): raise ValueError(...)`, and add a test case like `preview(tmp_path / "home", "../outside.txt")` that is expected to raise `ValueError`? — Any caller that passes user-supplied names to `preview` lets that user read any file the process can read, which defeats the "outside home" check this PR adds.
